did.unittitle: David Rockefeller Personal and Professional papers, Art Files of the David and Peggy Rockefeller Collection

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Open for research in accordance with the terms of donation from the David Rockefeller Estate, January 2019. Brittle or damaged items are available at the discretion of RAC.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Series 1 is art inventories from 1979. Series 2 is artist files for modern and impressionist art. Series 3 is curator files on all categories of art collected by David and Peggy Rockefeller. Series 4 is files on nonmodern art. Series 5 is documentation of porcelain, silver, and a range of furnishings. Series 6 documents decorative arts, as well as the inventories and appraisals within the art collection.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: David and Peggy Rockefeller collected artworks and decorative pieces from around the globe over the course of several decades. This collection documents their holdings and gives insight into their thoughts and practices regarding a life infused with art.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains inventories, mostly photographic, of the holdings and works within the David and Peggy Rockefeller art collection. The photo inventories typically are accompanied by the following information for each work: title, artist, period, provenance, acquisition information, and the collection identification number. Artist biographical sketches also exist for most of the modern art works. However, information on nonmodern art, porcelains, objects, and furniture comprises the bulk of this small series.

scopecontent.p: This series contains an alphabetical run of artist files for David and Peggy Rockefeller's collection of modern and impressionist art. Files typically include correspondence on acquisition of works, any conservation undertaken, exhibits or loans of individual pieces, valuations, and occasionally discussion of installations. If a work left the collection during David Rockefeller's lifetime, those details are also documented.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains documentation on works from a range of art periods that predate or fall outside the scope of impressionist and modern art (located in Series 2 of this collection). The region of origin and medium of each artwork also widely vary. Examples include early American works and folk art; European neoclassical or realist works; Chinese works; Japanese works; prints and lithographs; and traditional arts of indigenous peoples of Africa, North America, and the Middle East.

David Rockefeller's life-long interest in beetles is represented by a folder of decorative insect prints, which complemented his extensive sample collection. While some porcelain artworks are included in this series, most are located in Series 5 of these papers.

Files in this series typically include correspondence on acquisition of works, conservation efforts, exhibits or loans of individual pieces, and valuations. If a work left the collection during David Rockefeller's lifetime, those details are included.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series starts with documentation on David and Peggy Rockefeller's collection of porcelain, organized alphabetically by manufacturer, followed by porcelain inventories and valuations. The subsequent files cover silver, brass, furniture (including mirrors), glass, and lighting fixtures.

Files typically include correspondence on acquisition of pieces or sets, any restoration undertaken, exhibits or loans of individual pieces, valuations, and inventories. If an item left the collection during David Rockefeller's lifetime, those details are also documented. A few specific folders on appraisals and valuations have dates, but most files in this series are undated.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This final series of art documentation covers a range of works and pieces, such as decorative arts, carriages, decoys, rugs, pottery, and furniture. Many of these folders likely relate to the development and publication of relevant volumes of The David and Peggy Rockefeller Collection, the official set of catalogues of their extensive works. The series also contains decontructed binders of inventories, appraisals, and valuations of most of their art holdings. The inventory folders may be duplicates of those located in Series 1 of this collection.
